text:
Sam: Quick follow-up on private CP patterns. We keep oscillating between a DNS-overlay (split-horizon) vs pushing per-tenant private endpoints. Can we list non-obvious operational harms for the DNS-overlay?
Marta: DNS-overlay is easiest for incremental rollout and lets us keep a single control-plane hostname. But it forces split-horizon DNS and makes cert/SNI semantics subtle. Also harder to prove traffic path for customers.
Devin: From infra side, split-horizon means cache invalidation and stale resolution are the big risks. Users hitting old ENIs during a failover shows up as 5xx until DNS flips.
Liz: Security: with DNS-overlay we still need connector-auth (mTLS) to the control plane. But SNI-based routing + cert pinning is more brittle. With per-tenant endpoints the customer can see a distinct SAN and that's better for audit logs.
Shreyas: Implementation note: if we prefer DNS-overlay, we must add an active invalidation path that triggers on failover so clients don't rely only on TTL. TTL-only is not enough for enterprise SLOs.
Sam: What about a hybrid: control-plane DNS-overlay for bootstrap, then connectors publish a per-tenant endpoint in the customer's VPC that we surface in Console as the canonical endpoint. Clients can choose to pin to the ENI for low-latency tenants.
Marta: Hybrid seems attractive: it keeps the simple DNS migration story but offers an explicit lifecycle for per-tenant endpoints. Console needs a field for endpoint_fingerprint + endpoint_ip + visibility whether customer has pinned.
Devin: That requires connector lifecycle ownership decisions — who rotates certs on the ENI? If Redwood rotates, we can push changes but must guarantee zero-downtime rotation. If customer rotates, our bootstrap token flow must support re-registration.
Liz: Proposal: connectors must expose /meta (json with cert_fingerprint, version), /healthz, and an admin path /rotate that accepts a short-lived bootstrap token. Connector MUST present its cert fingerprint during bootstrap and on every health check.
Sam: Example bootstrap config: 
```
redwood.bootstrap_token_ttl=300s
redwood.dns_overlay_ttl=15s
on_endpoint_fail: invalidate-dns-cache -> mark-stale-in-console
```
Marta: Add a Console status enum: healthy, stale-dns, cert-mismatch, degraded. Alerting: enterprise pager on stale-dns > 30m, self-serve email after 24h.
Devin: For invalidation, we should prefer an evented approach: connector -> controlplane emits "endpoint-changed" -> dns-service invalidates and publishes tombstone A-record with very short TTL for 60s, then republish new record. That avoids hammering upstream resolvers.
Shreyas: Also need routing priority baked into the bootstrap: [eni_direct, regional_relay, public_fallback]. If connector signals eni_direct down, controlplane should shift to relay immediately and publish DNS changes.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: connector v1.3 canary scheduled Wednesday 03:00 UTC (2h window). Tag: canary-connector-v1.3
Liz: One UX corner: how do we surface a DNS pinning problem where customer-side resolvers cache an A record incorrectly? Recommend we instrument a per-tenant last_successful_ip and last_bootstrap_fingerprint so Console can show a mismatch hint.
Sam: Good. Make action items:
- Shreyas: add /meta and /rotate endpoints to connector spec and design robust rotate handshake (auth + replay protection).
- Devin: prototype DNS tombstone flow + metrics for propagation time and stale-hit-rate.
- Marta: add Console fields (endpoint_ip, endpoint_fingerprint, last_seen, status) and alerting thresholds.
- Liz (security): publish termination rules: when SNI mismatch -> immediate reject; when fingerprint mismatch -> flag + failover to relay per policy.
Marta: Will open Console PR by EOD Thursday.
Sam: Let's review in arch sync Friday. If we accept hybrid, we should write a short RFC that formalizes the bootstrap token lifecycle and the DNS tombstone behavior.
Liz: I'll draft the RFC sections for security and SNI cert semantics.
Sam: Thanks all.
